title: refactor(ci): unify lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache parallelism
author: Ethan Zhang
description:
Motivation: The repo has accumulated multiple slightly different CI workflows for lint, unit/integration tests, and release automation. This causes duplicated matrix runs, inconsistent caching, and makes maintaining action versions harder. This change consolidates the workflows into a smaller set of unified files, standardizes Node/tool versions, and introduces a controlled cache-parallelism strategy to reduce CI bottlenecks.

What this PR does: consolidates .github/workflows/lint.yml, test.yml, and release.yml into two workflow families (lint-test.yml and release.yml with shared reusable workflows); upgrades actions and moves the primary Node runtime to 20.x (aligned with infra plans); centralizes cache key patterns and adds a parallel cache warmup step to allow multiple caches to be warmed in parallel rather than sequentially; removes duplicated matrix entries across packages; standardizes environment variables and secrets references to GH_* conventions; documents migration notes for local contributors.

Checklist:
- [x] Consolidate lint & test into reusable workflows and reduce duplicated matrices
- [x] Upgrade GH Actions used by workflows to latest non-breaking minor versions
- [x] Implement cache parallelism with controlled fan-out (defaults tuned to our runners)
- [x] Validate important repositories (redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-sdk-typescript) on forked runners
- [x] Add migration notes in docs/ci.md and updated runbooks

Testing and validation: ran the unified workflows on branch and verified successful runs across representative repo matrices. Observed ~28-35% reduction in median CI wall time on the test suite for the monorepo CI pipeline (most savings from cache warmup parallelism and removing duplicate matrix axes). One flaky integration test (packages/redwood-helm-charts/test/deploy.test.ts) was unstable on first run; re-run succeeded after test timeout increase and minor mocking fix included in a follow-up commit.

Rollout plan: Merge to main gated behind 2 reviewers. Monitor first 24 hours of CI runs for unexpected failures; we have a rollback plan to re-enable legacy workflows if we see regression in release automation. Release automation (publish workflows) kept separate to minimize blast radius for publishing changes.

Rollback: Revert commit and re-enable previous workflow YAML files (they are backed up under .github/legacy/).

Notes for reviewers: focus on cache key patterns, matrix reductions, and the parallelism fanout parameter. If you need to tune for different runner pools, the fanout is configurable via workflow_dispatch inputs and repository secrets.

d9a2f0b: docs(ci): add migration notes and runbook for unified workflows
changes_snippets: .github/workflows/lint-test.yml: added reusable jobs and reduced matrix axes to {node: [20], os: [ubuntu-latest]}

YAML snippet: 'uses: ./.github/actions/cache-warmup
with:
  cache-keys: ${{ fromJson(inputs.cache_keys) }}
  parallelism: ${{ inputs.parallelism }}'
scripts/ci/cache.sh: unified cache key generation across packages; example key: 'node-modules-${{ matrix.pkg }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}'

Omar Haddad (review): Found one action pin that used a floating major. I updated to a pinned minor version and added an integration test to ensure action runs are stable.
